title: Row-end increases — adding stitches at the edge
subtitle: Work extra stitches at the row start or end to widen the piece intentionally
excerpt: Row-end increases add one or more stitches at the beginning or end of a row, widening the piece. The two main methods are: working 2 stitches into the edge stitch, or turning-chain increases that add extra stitches before the first row stitch. Both are standard shaping techniques for garments, triangles, and shawls.

glossaryTerms.definition: An increase worked at the start or end of a crochet row to add stitch width. At the end of a row: work 2 stitches into the final stitch. At the start: work extra turning chains and use them as new stitches, or work 2 dc into the first stitch.

heroPrompt: A triangular crochet swatch in sage green DK yarn, worked from bottom point up, showing the widening rows from increases at both edges, close-up.

content.text: is the standard way to widen a piece that is worked back and forth. The method depends on which end needs the increase and how many stitches are to be added. A single stitch at each end is by far the most common — it produces a smooth diagonal edge used in sleeve shaping and triangle shawl panels.
Increasing at the end of a row
Work to the last stitch of the row.
Work 2 dc (or tr, htr — whatever stitch the row uses) into the final stitch. One stitch added at the end edge.
Increasing at the start of a row (chain method)
At the end of the previous row, instead of turning, ch 2 extra (for a dc row: ch 3 instead of ch 1; for a tr row: ch 4 instead of ch 3).
Turn. Work a dc into the 2nd ch from hook (for dc row) — this creates one new stitch before the main row begins.
Continue across the row normally. One stitch added at the start edge.

items.symptom: The edge develops a stepped instead of diagonal look
items.cause: Adding increases only at the end of every other row rather than both edges and both rows
items.fix: For a smooth diagonal, increase both edges on every row (or on specified rows per the pattern). Unequal spacing creates steps rather than a continuous slope.

content.text: For mid-row increases — adding width inside a row rather than at the edges — work 2 stitches into any single stitch at the required position. Raglan shaping uses a paired mid-row increase at four positions within each round.
